oil.summary: A brutal session for crude saw Brent shed 8.56% to $97.47/bbl and WTI drop 2.29% to $92.44/bbl, opening a near-$12 Brent-WTI spread that headlines attribute to soaring freight costs and dislocated Atlantic Basin flows stemming from the ongoing Iran conflict. The Strait of Hormuz remains partially blockaded — Iran has stated the closure continues until attacks end — while Trump has threatened to escalate strikes. Some relief came from a reported temporary US easing of Russia oil sanctions, though European allies are reportedly furious. RBOB gasoline was the session's hardest hit, collapsing 10.32%, while heating oil fell 3.18% despite diesel crunch fears. Capitol Hill is pressing for tougher action against Chinese entities purchasing Iranian barrels, and Aramco's partial restart of its East-West pipeline provided only modest comfort. CME OPEC Watch prices a 77% chance of a cut at the next meeting.
drivers: Strait of Hormuz blockade persists; Iran conditions reopening on cessation of attacks, keeping geopolitical premium in Brent but distorting WTI differentials via freight and rerouting costs
US temporarily eases Russia oil sanctions to cap price surge, angering European allies; Trump simultaneously threatens 100% tariffs on Indian and Chinese buyers of Russian crude
RBOB gasoline cratered 10.32% on the day; diesel crunch fears and Italy pushing refineries to boost output signal downstream stress across Atlantic markets

gas.summary: Natural gas markets saw a modest pullback Friday, with Henry Hub slipping 1.40% to $3.251/MMBtu after an 11.64% weekly surge, while TTF fell 4.03% to €72.08/MWh, giving back some of its recent war-risk premium. On the supply side, Saudi Aramco's partial restoration of the East-West Petroline pipeline — knocked out less than two weeks ago — eased some Gulf supply anxiety. In Europe, the EU's Gas Coordination Group indicated supply remains stable despite low storage levels, helping cap TTF. A separate note highlighted that despite record Lower 48 heat over the summer, Henry Hub averaged only $2.93/MMBtu June–August, underscoring structural oversupply limiting upside. Baker Hughes data showed a week-on-week rise in active US oil and gas rigs, pointing to a supply response beginning to take shape under elevated prices.
drivers: Aramco's partial Petroline restart eases immediate Gulf gas and liquids supply fears, contributing to TTF's 4% daily pullback
EU Gas Coordination Group signals stable European supply despite low storage, tempering panic buying even as the Iran conflict lingers
Rising US rig count and evidence that summer heat failed to structurally lift Henry Hub suggest ample domestic supply; Henry Hub weekly gain of 11.6% may be running ahead of fundamentals

power.summary: Power and carbon markets were relatively contained on Friday. EU EUAs edged up 0.90% to $82.46/EUA, extending a modest weekly and monthly grind higher, consistent with elevated gas prices feeding through to carbon costs in the power stack even as TTF eased on the day. Headline flow for the sector was thin on direct power market news; the most notable item was India weighing mandatory imported coal blending at power plants as domestic stocks deteriorate amid logistics issues — a potential demand signal for seaborne coal. Trump's threat to halt US diesel exports rattled UK markets and added a secondary supply-security concern for European power operators reliant on distillate backup generation. Nigeria's IEA membership alongside a six-year output high was noted but carries limited near-term power market read-through.
drivers: EUAs nudge higher (+0.90%) as elevated gas prices sustain carbon costs in the European power mix, even with TTF pulling back intraday
India weighing mandatory imported coal blending signals potential tightening of seaborne thermal coal supply with knock-on effects for Asian and European power fuel costs
Trump's threatened US diesel export halt puts UK and European backup power generation economics at risk, adding a supply-security layer to an already stressed continental energy picture
